title: House Robber II
summary: You plan to rob houses in a circular street.
statement: You plan to rob houses in a circular street. Each house has a specific amount of money. Houses are adjacent and have connected security systems. If two adjacent houses are robbed, the police are alerted. Given an array of house values, determine the maximum money that can be robbed without triggering an alert.
constraints: Houses form a circle: the first and last are adjacent. Choose no two adjacent houses; choosing none is allowed. A single house may be chosen.
hints: A valid choice cannot contain both endpoints of the array.
Solve two linear ranges: one excludes the first house and the other excludes the last.
Within each range track the best totals for the previous two positions; return the larger range answer, handling a singleton separately.
Use index ranges rather than slices to keep auxiliary storage constant.
editorial: Every valid circular selection omits at least one endpoint, so the two linear subproblems cover all possibilities. Each linear range uses the choose-or-skip recurrence with two running values. The independent oracle enumerates every subset of small circular inputs and explicitly rejects adjacent selected positions, including the wraparound edge. The singleton special case avoids treating a house as its own forbidden neighbor.

tests.explanation: The two outer 2s are neighbors around the circle and cannot both be chosen; the best total is the middle 3.
Choose positions 0 and 2 for total 4; they are not adjacent, and the final house is skipped.
